A1.justification: Both versions describe OlaMind's expert-reasoning distillation and staged SFT/RL framework. The main text, figures, tables, equations and complete appendices (v1 A–C; v2 A–G) support comparison. The changed title and expanded scope do not obscure the work's identity.

before.justification: v1 reports original offline comparisons, reward ablations, online A/B results and human GSB evaluation, including Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 reports original OLABENCH evaluations, human–judge validation, latency and rubric analyses, human assessments and online experiments.

M1.justification: The underlying distillation and alternating SFT/GRPO stages remain despite renaming. However, v2 adds instance-specific rubric generation and rewards (Algorithm 1), policy-compliance and tool-calling objectives, and explicitly excludes safety penalties from Stage-1, whereas v1's basic RL includes risk evaluation. Length and hallucination reward weights also change from 0.5/5 to 1/3.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates RAG-based customer-service dialogue. v2's OLABENCH-CORE includes 768 RAG, 952 workflow and 1,280 agent instances, alongside risk and hallucination subsets (Table 1). Predefined workflow execution and autonomous tool use substantially extend the evaluated task requirements.

E2.justification: The main comparator roster changes substantially between v1 Table 2 and v2 Table 3: GPT-5/Gemini 2.5 Pro become GPT-5.2/Gemini 3 Pro, and newer Kimi, DeepSeek-V3 and Qwen variants replace earlier ones. Both Doubao comparators and the explicit distilled baseline disappear; untuned Qwen3-8B/14B baselines are added. DeepSeek-R1 remains, and Figure 6 introduces a no-rubric control.

E3.justification: v2 introduces policy-compliance, tool-calling, latency and Overall metrics, revises dialogue-quality and hallucination criteria, and changes service-quality judging to Doubao-Seed-1.6. Core evaluation grows from 1,000 to 3,000 instances. Reported training sizes also change: cold-start SFT 432K to 363K, re-cold-start SFT 152K to 250K, and the two RL stages 17K/15K to 52K each.

E4.justification: v2 adds judge-validation analyses, pre/post-CoT efficiency comparisons, risk/hallucination type breakdowns, a rubric-control training analysis and intent-stratified online evaluation (Section 3.3, Figures 4–6, Appendix B). v1's four reward-component ablations and human-likeness score histogram are removed. Existing conversation examples are largely retained in v2 Figure 8.

E5.justification: v1 primarily reports point estimates. v2 adds online A/B p-values, human–judge Spearman correlations, 95% inter-annotator agreement, and training-reward standard deviations and ranges. These substantially expand statistical reporting, but neither version supplies repeated-training seeds or confidence intervals; the added reporting does not establish additional training runs.

E6.justification: v1's offline results are replaced by OLABENCH results, including 78.72 Overall for Qwen3-14B Stage-2 versus 70.58/70.84 for GPT-5.2/Gemini 3 Pro (v2 Table 3). Changed data, metrics and backbones prevent interpreting these as cross-version performance gains. Aggregate online IRR/HTR gains remain unchanged. New results include Turing-test outcomes, latency speedups, judge agreement and intent-level online scores.

T1.justification: v2 introduces a normalization-and-averaging definition for its Overall score (Section 5.1), which has no counterpart in v1. The piecewise length-penalty definition remains equivalent apart from notation. Neither version contains theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: v1 primarily contributes a human-like, hallucination-safe RAG training framework. v2 makes OLABENCH a co-primary contribution and presents a benchmark-to-optimization loop spanning RAG, workflows and agents, with rubric-aware training and deployment-efficiency claims. Its headline online averages summarize retained results rather than stronger online outcomes.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations involving Stage-1 over-exploration, safety–service tradeoffs, rubric-guided stability and latency-sensitive reasoning. Its limitations replace v1's workflow/multi-agent instruction-following and long-range planning concerns with unverified legal/counseling generalization, rubric-generation overhead and text-only coverage (v1 Appendix C; v2 Section 7).

D1.justification: v2 adds benchmark-construction procedures, annotation protocols and counts, full-parameter tuning disclosure, dialogue statistics, and policy/tool/rubric/CoT evaluation prompts (Appendices A, C, D, F and G). v1's Volcengine Ark disclosure and promised future code/data release are absent. This removes an access commitment, without establishing that previously available artifacts were withdrawn.

R1.justification: v2 repositions the work around industrial benchmarking, adding discussion of tau-bench, TeleEval-OS, ECom-Bench and MultiChallenge. It removes v1's dedicated RAG survey, including UniMS-RAG, CRAG and Speculative RAG, and explicitly positions its rubric method relative to Rubrics as Rewards in Appendix F.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and conclusion are extensively rewritten. A benchmark section now precedes the method; training stages are renamed and reorganized; related work is restructured; and appendix material is redistributed across A–G. Limitations move into the main text, and an ethical-considerations section is added.

P2.justification: v2 replaces the introductory/framework illustrations with a combined overview, restructures the main results table, and adds benchmark-statistics, annotation and intent tables plus latency and diagnostic plots. The old reward-ablation and score-distribution displays disappear. Retained examples are relocated and relabeled, including v1 Figure 7 becoming v2 Figure 8; appendix prompts and rubric examples receive new layouts.

improvement.justification: Human–judge validation, detector-accuracy checks and detailed annotation protocols strengthen the empirical assessability that v1 lacked. Latency measurements also substantiate deployment claims. The gain is limited by removal of v1's controlled reward ablations and unresolved inconsistencies: v2 Figure 5 reports 17.4% Stage-2 overcommitting, exceeding either Stage-2 total risk rate in Table 3 without explaining different settings. These weaknesses temper the substantial expansion.
